text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Financial Stabilisation Council is expected to discuss today options for pegging the lev to the dollar or the mark under a planned currency board system, chairman of the parliament's budget committee Yordan Tsonev said.
-- The Yugoslav State Railways will start repaying some $15 million of debt to the Bulgarian State Railways from Octeber 1, a visiting Yugoslav railway official said.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to discuss today lifting the current ban on grain exports in line with Bulgaria's pledges to liberalise its trade regulations, the Agiculture ministry said. Grain exports were banned in 1995 because of a wheat shortage.
-- Bulgaria's Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan said it has posted 471 million lev gross profit in 1996. @
-- Bulgaria's VIS-2 insurance company said it had a 88.5 million lev net profit for last year.

-- Bulgaria's commercial banks internal credit fell by 65.9 billion levs in the second week of May to 3.888 trillion levs, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
